scope: Lane A's seven new method bodies, original owner refinements and metadata. Independent instruction/application review only; no product adoption or release claim.

findings.title: The recurring-revenue bridge restricts entrant events to the opening customer population
findings.problem: The instruction says to use mutually exclusive events over the same opening customer population, then adds new and reactivated accounts. Those accounts can be outside that population. The method later distinguishes losses from the opening base, so the conflation can omit growth or contaminate cohort retention.
findings.counterexample: Opening 200, new 40, expansion 30, reactivation 20, contraction 10, churn 70 closes at 210. Restricting event membership to the opening population closes at 150, leaving 60 unexplained. Opening-cohort net retention is 75%, not 105%.
findings.repair: Use one business/reporting scope and interval with opening run rate as baseline. Explicitly count new and reactivated entrants outside the opening cohort; keep opening-cohort retention calculations restricted to that cohort. Retain mutually exclusive event classification and separate currency/scope adjustments.
findings.verification: Keep the independent four-account fixture and reconcile both the whole-scope 210 close and opening-cohort 150 close/75% retention without inserting a retention ratio as another event.
findings.owner: parent or lane A; reviewer has no product write authority

findings.title: Three new methods lack useful discovery cues in their owner metadata
findings.problem: The real searchCatalog consumer, with the seven reviewed/final owner metadata snapshots overlaid on the unchanged 93-skill catalog, misses intended owners in four direct/paraphrase top-five probes.
